title: Ending a closed subject leaves hope

captions.energy: Trying talk without a prepared result
captions.emotions: Feeling hope for a new continuation

meaning: You can end a formula that closes a subject in advance and freely try another beginning, preserving hope without promising immediately matching interests.
text: Death in the physical position of your Vishuddha appears in ending words that closed a subject beforehand. The Fool in energy supports willingness to try conversation without a prepared result or familiar roles. The Star in emotions brings hope for another continuation. You can leave an earlier answer and hear what happens now. An open perspective requires neither identical interest in advance nor guaranteed success in the first new exchange.

For example, you stop saying “Talking about poetry is not for us” when you want to share one line that appealed. Instead, you directly offer to explain why it stayed in memory. **A new subject can begin without promising to interest both people**. You hear a genuine question or an honest lack of interest. Hope remains a possibility of discovering each other rather than an obligation to love the same thing. Ending a shared prohibition neither assigns every following evening to this subject nor requires proving the change useful.

Expectation becomes rigid if the new perspective permits only encouragement in response. An earlier closing script then becomes another in which quiet lack of interest is forbidden. The Fool’s constructive openness helps leave the result unknown. You can offer something unfamiliar and hear different responses; hope supports conversation when another subject remains possible and an unsuccessful first attempt does not prove the old prohibition right.
